## Competition guides

### NACLO — North American Computational Linguistics Olympiad
- Held annually in late January (Open Round) and March (Invitational)
- Open to US and Canadian high school students
- Problems focus on linguistic reasoning; no prior linguistics knowledge required
- [Official site](https://nacloweb.org) · [Past problems](https://nacloweb.org/resources/problems/)

### NACLI — North American Computational Linguistics Invitational
- The invitation-only team round following the NACLO Invitational
- Five-person teams, collaborative problems
- [Past NACLI problems](https://nacloweb.org)

### IOL — International Linguistics Olympiad
- Held annually in July/August
- Individual and team rounds
- Problems are harder and more linguistically sophisticated than NACLO
- [Official site](https://ioling.org) · [Problem archive](https://ioling.org/problems/)

---

## Study strategy

### For beginners
1. Work through all NACLO Open problems from 2015–2018
2. Focus on morphology first — it's the most common type
3. Learn the IPA (International Phonetic Alphabet) basics
4. Practice writing out your reasoning step by step

### For advanced competitors
1. Study IOL problems from 2010 onwards
2. Learn basic formal language theory (for computational problems)
3. Read a linguistics textbook — *Language Files* (Ohio State) is excellent
4. Practice under timed conditions

## Useful references

| Resource | Use |
|----------|-----|
| [IPA Chart](https://www.internationalphoneticassociation.org/content/ipa-chart) | Phone reference for phonology problems |
| [WALS Online](https://wals.info) | World Atlas of Language Structures — great for checking typological patterns |
| [Glottolog](https://glottolog.org) | Language family tree and basic info |
| *Language Files* (11th ed.) | Comprehensive introductory textbook |
| *The Study of Language* (Yule) | Gentler introduction |

## Export to PDF / Book {#export}

This site is built with Quarto, which can also render to PDF and LaTeX. To generate a printable problem book:

```bash
# Render the full site to PDF
quarto render --to pdf

# Or render just one file
quarto render problems/2024/swahili-verbs.qmd --to pdf

# Generate a book (requires _quarto.yml set to type: book)
quarto render --to pdf
```

### Creating a LaTeX book

To export as a proper LaTeX book for further customization, switch the project type in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  type: book

book:
  title: "Linguistics Olympiad Problem Collection"
  author: "Your Name"
  chapters:
    - index.qmd
    - problems/2024/swahili-verbs.qmd
    - problems/2023/devanagari.qmd
```

Then run `quarto render --to latex` to get a `.tex` file you can compile with any LaTeX distribution.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Online LaTeX editing
Use [Overleaf](https://overleaf.com) to edit and compile the exported LaTeX without installing anything locally — just upload the `.tex` file and any assets.
:::

## Contributing problems

This site is open source. To add a problem:

1. Fork the repository on GitHub
2. Copy the template from `problems/_template.qmd`
3. Fill in the problem data, hints, and solution
4. Open a pull request

See `CONTRIBUTING.md` in the repository for full guidelines.
